objectives: Prepare and register a notarial invitation in the right number of copies.
Serve a document at an address following the Civil Procedure Code: personally, through another person, or by posting a notice.
Record each visit so that the service holds up in court.
Draw up a declaratory protocol of appearance or non-appearance.
Accept documents for safekeeping and return them correctly.

cards.front: In how many copies is a notarial invitation presented?
Who keeps the three copies after the service?
cards.back: One for the **requester**, one in the notary's **book**, one for the **addressee** ([[gpk:592:1]]).
An **employee** whom the notary assigns, under [[gpk:37|Art. 37]]–[[gpk:58|58 ГПК]] ([[znnd:50]]).

cards.front: The server finds only the addressee's 16-year-old daughter at home. May she receive the invitation?
cards.back: **No**. Only an **adult** household member or person living at the address, or a worker, employee or employer of the addressee, who **agrees**, may receive it ([[gpk:46:2]]).

cards.front: When may the server post a notice?
cards.back: When the addressee cannot be found for **one month** and nobody agrees to receive the paper ([[gpk:47:1]]).

cards.front: How is it established that the addressee cannot be found?
cards.back: At least **three visits**, at least **one week** apart, at least **one on a non-working day** ([[gpk:47:1]]).

cards.front: How long may the addressee collect the papers after a notice is posted?
cards.back: **Two weeks**; the service is deemed made when the term expires ([[gpk:47:2|Art. 47(2)]], [[gpk:47:5|(5) ГПК]]).

cards.front: The addressee opens the door and refuses to take the invitation. Is the service valid?
cards.back: **Yes**. The server notes the refusal and certifies it with a signature ([[gpk:44:1]]).

cards.front: The server finds the company's office locked and nobody who agrees to receive the papers. What now?
cards.back: The server posts a notice under [[gpk:47:1|Art. 47(1)]]; a **second notice is not posted** ([[gpk:50:4]]).

cards.front: What does a declaratory protocol certify?
cards.back: The **appearance or non-appearance** of persons before the notary, and their consent or disagreement ([[gpk:593]]).

cards.front: How is a deposit of documents recorded?
cards.back: An **acceptance protocol** in two copies; on the return, a **handover protocol** ([[gpk:594]]).

cards.front: What is the fee for a notarial invitation?
cards.back: **20 лв. (10.23 €)**; the other copies as copies; half for a service ex officio ([[tarifa:3|item 3 ТНТ]]).

quiz.question: A co-owner wants to prove that he offered his share to his sister on the same terms. Which notarial act fits best?
options: A notarial invitation served on the sister
A declaratory deed of ownership of the share
A certified copy of the offer to the sister
A declaratory protocol of her non-appearance
quiz.explanation: [[zs:33]]: before a sale to a third person the co-owner presents written evidence that he offered the share to the other co-owners on the same terms; a notarial invitation ([[gpk:592]]) certifies that the offer was communicated. A copy proves only the text, not its communication.

quiz.question: The server finds the addressee's 15-year-old son at home. May the server leave the invitation with him?
options: No; the other person must be an adult
Yes; any household member may receive it
Yes, if the son signs the receipt for it
Yes, if a parent agrees by telephone
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:46:2]]: the other person may be any adult household member or person living at the address, or a worker, employee or employer of the addressee, who agrees to receive the paper. A minor cannot receive it, even with a signature.

quiz.question: The addressee is never at home. What is the minimum before posting a notice?
options: Three visits over a month, one on a non-working day
Two visits on working days, at least one week apart
Three visits in one week, one of them in the evening
One visit and a registered letter with a return receipt
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:47:1]]: the addressee cannot be found when the server made at least three visits over one month, at least one week apart, at least one on a non-working day, and found nobody who agrees to receive the paper. Only then is the notice posted.

quiz.question: The condominium manager says the addressee moved abroad two years ago. What does the server do?
options: Notes the statement and its source; the visit rule does not apply
Ignores it; only the three visits at the address count in court
Posts the notice at once, without noting the manager's statement
Returns the invitation to the requester as not served at the address
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:47:1]]: the rule on the three visits does not apply when the server collected data that the addressee does not live at the address and noted the source of the data. The statement and its source go into the record of the service.

quiz.question: When is the invitation deemed served after a notice was posted?
options: When the two-week term for collecting it expires
On the day the notice was posted on the door
One month after the notice was posted on the door
Only when the addressee collects the invitation
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:47:2]]: the notice states that the papers can be collected within two weeks of the posting; [[gpk:47:5|Art. 47(5)]]: the paper is deemed served when that term expires, whether or not the addressee collects it.

quiz.question: The addressee opens the door but refuses to take the invitation. What happens?
options: The server notes and certifies the refusal; the service is valid
The service fails; the invitation goes back to the requester
The server calls the police to witness and certify the refusal
The server returns next week and tries a second time at the door
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:44:1]]: the server certifies with a signature the date and the way of the service and all actions related to it, including a refusal; the refusal does not affect the validity of the service. No police and no second visit are needed.

quiz.question: Where is an invitation to an OOD served?
options: At the last address in the register, to any employee who agrees
At the home address of the manager, to the manager in person
At the address of its bank, to the account manager of the company
At the office of the tax agency, to the clerk of the company's file
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:50:1]]: a company is served at the last address stated in its register; [[gpk:50:3|Art. 50(3)]]: in its office, to any employee or worker who agrees to receive the paper. The server notes the name and position of the receiver.

quiz.question: The buyer came at the agreed time to sign the final deed; the seller did not. Which act proves this?
options: A declaratory protocol of appearance
A notarial invitation to the seller
A declaratory deed of the agreement
A certification of the date of the draft
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:593]]: a declaratory protocol certifies the appearance or non-appearance of persons before the notary for an act, and the consent or disagreement of those who appeared. An invitation only calls the seller; it does not prove his absence.

quiz.question: The server posted a notice at the locked office of a company. Three weeks later nobody collected the papers. Does the server post a second notice?
options: No; for a company a second notice is not posted
Yes; a second notice starts a new two-week term
Yes; the notice is posted again after one month
No; the papers are sent to the home of the manager
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:50:4]]: when the server finds no access to the office and nobody who agrees to receive the paper, a notice is posted under [[gpk:47:1|Art. 47(1)]], and a second notice is not posted. The service is deemed made when the two-week term expires ([[gpk:47:5|Art. 47(5)]]).

quiz.question: The invitation was handed to a neighbour who does not live at the address. He gave it to the addressee the next day. When is the service made?
options: On the day the invitation actually reached the addressee
Never; the service is void and must be repeated from the start
On the day the neighbour received the invitation
Two weeks after the neighbour received the invitation
quiz.explanation: A neighbour who does not live at the address is not an "other person" under [[gpk:46:2]], so the service is irregular. [[gpk:54|Art. 54]]: an irregular service is deemed made at the moment the paper actually reached the addressee, here the next day.

quiz.question: Who may take back deposited documents after the depositor died?
options: The heirs or a special agent, with a handover protocol
Any relative who presents the acceptance protocol to the notary
The notary keeps them until a court orders the return
Only a court, by a decision in the succession case
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:594:2]]: the return is recorded in a handover protocol signed by the depositor or, after the death, by the heirs or by a special agent; the protocol is entered in the register. A relative who is not an heir cannot take the documents.

quiz.question: Which person may NOT receive the invitation for the addressee?
options: The opposing party of the addressee in the same matter
The adult daughter of the addressee, who lives with him
The employer of the addressee, at the place of work
An adult tenant who lives at the address of the addressee
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:46:2]]: a paper is not served through a person who is the opposing party of the addressee. The adult daughter, the employer and an adult person living at the address are "other persons" who may receive it when they agree.
